title: Evacuation Planning That Actually Includes Everyone

body.en: Your neighbourhood is planning its flood evacuation route. One resident, Mr. Owusu, uses a wheelchair, and the route the group first proposed goes down a narrow alley with three steps at the end. What should happen next?

choices.label: Walk the proposed route with Mr. Owusu before finalising it, and adjust it based on what he finds
choices.consequence: Exactly right. A route that fails one resident during an actual flood isn't a backup plan — it's a plan that quietly excludes someone. Testing it with the people it needs to work for is how you catch that before it matters.

choices.label: Finalise the route as planned — Mr. Owusu can find his own way separately
choices.consequence: This leaves a real gap. An evacuation plan that only works for some residents isn't a complete plan — during an actual flood, 'find his own way' can mean not getting out in time.

choices.label: Assume someone will carry him if it comes to that
choices.consequence: Not a plan. Relying on an assumption that goes untested until the actual emergency is exactly how evacuation plans fail the people who need them most.
